subject.title: Feature: Multi-index embedding memory with model-aware failover (no mixed vector spaces)

question: Should memory-core add first-class multi-index embedding configuration/storage/status, and what rollout and doctor-migration contract should existing users get?
rationale: The request crosses public config, persisted SQLite schema, provider failover policy, plugin-memory boundaries, and operator observability; automation cannot safely choose that API shape.

options.title: Sponsor multi-index v1
options.body: Define a maintainer-approved v1 contract for per-model indexes, dual ingestion, active/fallback routing, status output, and migration before implementation starts.

options.title: Defer to narrow repairs
options.body: Keep current single-index semantics and only fix narrower fallback recovery or warning bugs such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/96534.

options.title: Reject core surface
options.body: Decline new memorySearch config/storage surface for now and require a plugin/API design discussion if an external memory backend needs this capability.

recommendation.title: Sponsor multi-index v1
recommendation.body: Define a maintainer-approved v1 contract for per-model indexes, dual ingestion, active/fallback routing, status output, and migration before implementation starts.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue is currently assigned to osolmaz and recent commits by the same owner touched memory provider-failure and local-provider fallback behavior.
